newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower on profit taking.

text.p: A steep drop in heavyweight Telkom combined with profit taking in selected counters to drag down the Jakarta index on Tuesday, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 7.90 points, or 1.24 percent, to close at 626.68 points. Gainers led losers by 65 to 55, with 51 counters unchanged.

"I think trading on Wednesday will continue to be quiet with the index moving in a narrow-range as technically the market remains in a consolidation phase," Kim Effendy, a broker from PT Sassoon Securities Indonesia, said.
Brokers said the listing of another banking stock Bank Umum Servitia on Wednesday would only have a limited impact on the market as its capitalisation was relatively small.
"It will give some spice to the market but no big surprises are expected from this listing," a local broker said.
Brokers said that despite the weak market sentiment, some counters including Bank Negara Indonesia, Lippo Life, Lippo Securities made gains in a significant locally-led buying.
They said slow trading and the weak market sentiment led investors to take profits and this combined with the fall in Telkom to push the composite index down.
Asahimas, Mulia Industrindo, Bank International Indonesia and Citra Marga were among the losers on profit taking, they said.
Heavyweight Telkom fell 6.06 percent to 3,875 rupiah on a volume of 4.1 million shares after a lower closing price in New York overnight.
Brokers said the selling movement was also due to perception that it had reached its highs as well as continued speculation that Telkom might propose a second share offering next year.
Bank Negara Indonesia topped the active list with 50.2 million shares traded as it rose 25 rupiah to 1,375 rupiah.
Lippo Life rose 50 rupiah to 2,000 rupiah on 9.5 million shares, while Lippo Securities rose 75 rupiah to 1,700 rupiah on 5.6 million shares.
Brokers said glass maker Mulia Industrindo underwent a correction on profit taking despite news that the firm would increase the glass product prices in early 1997.
Mulia Industrindo fell 50 rupiah to 2,425 rupiah on a volume of five million shares.
